He came running up our driveway end of June of last year, 8/9 weeks old about 2 lbs, with the worst case of ringworm our vet had ever seen. 27 medicated baths, seven weeks of oral treatment, lots and lots and LOTS of later; you’d never know. 🥹

Why is my cat suddenly extremely obsessed with us So last night my 5 year old daughter managed to accidently spray perfume on my cat. As cats do, she tried to begin licking herself to clean it off. Since we were concerned about her ingesting the perfume, my wife gave her a bath in the tub. She didnt like the bath, but she didnt freak out and try to scratch her way out of it either. Ever since the bath and after she dried off, shes been extremely affectionate with us and obsessed with us. She slept right beside my wife all night and anytime we tried to move her from this spot, she would go right back to it (which is unlike her because usually she sleeps at the foot of the bed away from us by her own choosing or sleeps on a blanket on the floor). I woke up this morning and she has followed me to every single room I go into and keeps purring and wanting affection from me, which is again very unlike her. She's generally a very friendly and sociable cat, but since the bath she has increased her lovey doveyness by 100%. I'm not complaining because I love how sweet shes being, I just find it a little strange. Any reason she'd be doing this? She's the first cat I've had.

We found this poor little kitten in the woods, covered in ice, with her fur stuck to the hunk of plastic she was hiding under for shelter. We saved her 😁 Me and my kids were out exploring the fallen snow in the woods. We suddenly heard a cat meowing, over and over, it seemed to be in trouble. We finally found her under a random hunk of plastic laying there, she must have gotten under there for shelter. She was COMPLETELY covered in ice, and her fur was stuck to the side of the plastic thing she was hiding under, so she couldn't move. It was so sad, she's tiny, maybe 3-4 weeks old. We got her free and brought her home. We've been warming her up and feeding her, she's so happy now. Poor thing, if we hadn't just happened to go in that direction, we never would have found her, and she would have suffered and died there 😭 I was adamant we wouldn't go above 3 cats in the house again, but this one just feels like it was meant to be ours ❤️ Edits: WOW, I have never had a post blow up on Reddit before, this is crazy! A lot of people have expressed how nice it was to see something positive, during a rough time. I'm genuinely happy that I was able to bring something positive and uplifting to so many people's lives! This precious kitten definitely did that for us! This has been asked a lot. We HAVE returned to the spot we found her to see if we can find the mama cat, or any other kittens. We've been back twice so far, but nothing turned up. We plan to check again tomorrow. We plan to take her to a vet to get checked out as soon as the weather permits. For now, we're keeping her isolated from the rest of our cats. Her name is Elsa :) Edit 2: A lot of people were asking for updates and more pics, so I made an update post here: https://www.reddit.com/r/cats/comments/1qplxo5/updates_on_the_sweet_ice_princess_elsa/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button

Kitten lethargic after deworming My bf and I picked a kitty up off the street on Sunday took her to her first vet appt Thursday. Vet estimated her to be about 4 weeks. She was given dewormer at the vet and told me to come back in 2 weeks for her first round of shots. The day of her deworming, she ate fine, she played a little bit(definitely less than usual) and she seemed a little tired. It didn’t seem entirely out of the ordinary. Friday morning she ate her breakfast fine and seemed about the same as Thursday afternoon/night— not quite as playful but still pretty active. She wasn’t having diarrhea so I wasn’t sure if it just took a couple days to take effect? I just kept my eye on her until I left for work. However, Friday night she threw up one time and had some questionable looking stool, I assumed she was beginning to pass them. She did not play much at all, she seemed very sleepy. When she normally would play, she would just follow us around and whine/meow, it was starting to seem like she didn’t feel good. This morning, she had very loose stool and only wants to lie down. She will still follow us around but not too much, now will just lie down and go to sleep if we aren’t in the room with her. She hasn’t thrown up at all besides that one time. I’ve seen a lot of stuff about dewormer killing kittens and I’m a little worried. At what point do I stop scraping it up to the dewormer just doing what it’s supposed to be doing? I don’t want to make the judgement to call the vet too late.

Did I scar my cat for life? I really need some advice and reassurance, if possible. My 6 mo kitten got into one of my gift bags that had gifts for my friends from a trip, and she tore the bag apart and got stuck in the handle part of it (see video). I tried to get it off of her as I was scared that she would choke or get hurt. I cornered her because she's kind of a skiddish kitten and was able to rip the handle apart to free her. The problem is that she got super scared and hissed, and when I ripped the handle off, she scratched my hand like crazy. It's bleeding, but that's really not the problem for me. I'm more scared and sad of the possibility that she'll be scared of me forever now. I worked so hard these past couple of weeks since I got her to build a bond, and it seemed to be working, but I'm mad at myself for possibly resetting any progress I made with her :( Any advice or words of support?

Just out of curiosity, how often are you taking your healthy, indoor only cats to the vets for general checkups? First time cat mom here, so please be kind if there’s something I’m missing. I adopted two cats 7yrs and 10yrs December ‘25 and got them fully vetted afterwards and because that’s what the shelter recommended. We did extra bloodwork on the 10 yr old due to her age to check kidney values and both were perfectly healthy. This new vet recommends check ups every 6 months as a general recommendation because my cats are both a little older NOT because they have any health issues that require extra care. This seems excessive to me and just another way for them to make some money so I didn’t take them back at 6 months, and now they are emailing me to schedule another exam as it will have been one year in December. Money is a little tight so I think twice before I spend and try to avoid unnecessary expenses but ultimately I can afford vet care for my cats. I just don’t know if it’s necessary? I’m kind of leaning towards once every two years on the check ups and sick visits as needed. TLDR Are you taking your healthy indoor cats that are UTD on vaccinations to the vet yearly?? + a photo of my queen EDIT Thank you for the kind replies I will be taking both kitties in annually now that I understand the benefits
